$schema_note: Generated reference catalog for the OKF concept types defined in framework/method/metamodel/{requirements,architecture,design}.md and okf.md §9.2. Consumed by Workbench's spec-type badge (icon + hover description next to a concept file's `type:` frontmatter). Regenerate by hand when a concept type's definition changes in the source .md files — this file is a rendering aid, not a source of truth; the .md files remain authoritative.

domain.description: The overall business domain the application serves: its purpose, scope/boundaries, and the capabilities it decomposes into. One per application, an overview rather than a per-instance concept.

capability.description: A meaningful business ability or area of responsibility supported by the application.

entity.description: A durable business concept with identity, information, behavior, relationships, or lifecycle relevant to the application.

use-case.description: A structured behavioral specification describing how an actor or external trigger uses the system to achieve a meaningful goal. One file per use case.

workflow.description: A durable, end-to-end business process or lifecycle that sequences multiple use cases, actors, and states over time — spans more than one actor-triggered interaction.

business-rule.description: A durable business constraint, derivation, authorization, eligibility condition, or policy that governs business behavior.

role.description: A business responsibility or actor classification relevant to permissions or use cases.

page.description: An application-specific UI realization: purpose, users, presented information, inputs, actions, states, and navigation for one screen/page.

api-contract.description: An application-specific API endpoint/operation contract: request, response, validation, errors, and authorization.

integration.description: An application-specific integration with an external system: direction/protocol, data exchanged, trigger/timing, failure behavior, and security.

data-model.description: The physical/relational realization of the business entities and relationships within the chosen persistence technology. One per application, an overview rather than a per-instance concept.

architecture.description: A durable engineering decision or constraint affecting multiple features, components, or future changes: decision, rationale, constraints, consequences.
